questions.q: How do you define a DEFAULT inline on a column?
options: ColumnName type DEFAULT (value), written directly in CREATE TABLE
DEFAULT only works on PRIMARY KEY columns
DEFAULT must be written as its own CREATE DEFAULT statement
You can only add a DEFAULT with a separate ALTER TABLE statement
questions.explain: Writing DEFAULT (value) right after a column's type and nullability defines it inline, in the same CREATE TABLE statement.

questions.q: Exactly when does a DEFAULT constraint apply to an INSERT?
options: Only when the column is left out of the INSERT's column list entirely
Only on the very first row ever inserted into the table
Whenever the column receives any value, including an explicit NULL
Only when the table has no primary key
questions.explain: A DEFAULT kicks in for an omitted column. If you explicitly supply NULL, SQL Server inserts NULL rather than falling back to the default.

questions.q: What happens if you explicitly write NULL for a column that has a DEFAULT, instead of omitting the column?
options: SQL Server silently uses the DEFAULT value instead of NULL
The DEFAULT constraint is permanently removed from the column
SQL Server inserts NULL — the DEFAULT does not apply
The INSERT always fails with an error
questions.explain: DEFAULT only fills in for a column that's missing from the INSERT entirely, not one explicitly set to NULL.

questions.q: How do you add a DEFAULT constraint to a column on a table that already exists?
options: You cannot add a DEFAULT after CREATE TABLE — it must be inline
UPDATE every existing row to set the default value manually
DROP TABLE and recreate it with the default included
ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... DEFAULT (value) FOR ColumnName
questions.explain: ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT with a DEFAULT clause and FOR ColumnName attaches a default after the fact.

questions.q: Why name a default constraint explicitly, like DF_LessonDemo2_Status?
options: SQL Server requires a name or the ALTER TABLE statement fails
It gives you a predictable name to reference if you need to drop or change it later
Only named default constraints actually take effect
It automatically makes the column NOT NULL
questions.explain: Just like naming a primary key constraint, an explicit name avoids relying on SQL Server's harder-to-predict auto-generated name.
